item: a side file cut mid-character no longer ends a restore at the side-files stage
summary: merge_side_files caught (OSError, JSONDecodeError) around the calendar stores and OSError around the logs, so a staged member an earlier crash had cut in the middle of a multi-byte character raised UnicodeDecodeError (a ValueError) and ended the whole import at the side-files stage, before the live corpus was touched; the live store's loader had caught it since R397, the incoming side had not. A calendar store is now skipped and reported (unreadable in artifact). In a log member and the live log every line that is text is kept and a line that is NOT valid UTF-8 is withheld whole, never repaired, as the export side does (scrubbed_copy): it cannot be checked for the passphrase, and a repair that turns the bad bytes into U+FFFD left most of a held key in the live log (found by the independent read and proved by a test, then reworked). Each withheld line leaves one sentence that counts its bytes (never deduplicated, never counted as a duplicate), the log's report entry carries undecodable_lines_withheld only when it is above zero, and the fallback splits where a clean read does (surrogateescape plus str.splitlines). src/backup/merge.py only (the calendar except, new _log_lines and _withheld_sentence, the log loop). 13 new tests, 10 red on main (8 with UnicodeDecodeError at the three read sites, 2 on the new helper's name), 3 controls; 18 mutants killed. Stated limits: a torn tail already in the live log stays in the file (appends land after it); restoring the same artifact twice writes the sentences a second time; a sentence's byte count leaves out the line ending (the export's counts it). Not seen in the field: driven by tests that cut the files. Not changed here: a calendar store holding a lone-surrogate JSON escape, or valid JSON of the wrong shape, also ended the stage; it was closed separately in events/feeds.py by #1707.
